evaluations.reasoning: None of the candidate chunks explain the political strategy of forestalling rebellions and hearing smallfolk grievances during Aegon I's royal progresses.
Rank 5 describes Queen Visenya as a grim, stern, and unforgiving warrior rumored to practice dark arts and poisons, contrasting her with her sister.
Rank 3 explains the Doctrine of Exceptionalism, stating that Valyrian descent and dragonriding set Targaryens apart from other men and exempt them from Faith prohibitions against incest.
None of the candidate chunks mention the thematic motivation of the Winter Wolves seeking death in battle to avoid burdening their kin during winter.
None of the candidate chunks discuss the green council's specific fear of the court becoming a brothel under Prince Daemon and Rhaenyra.
Rank 1 describes Aegon III as the Broken King, characterizing him as a joyless, enigmatic monarch steeped in lifelong grief and melancholy.
None of the candidate chunks explain the specific underlying cause that precipitated the First Quarrel between Jaehaerys and Alysanne.
Rank 2 details how the multiple weddings of 49 AC (the Year of the Three Brides) produced mutual resentment and estrangement among Jaehaerys, Queen Alyssa, and Lord Rogar.
Rank 1 portrays the Shepherd as a religious populist and anti-dragon leader who held sway over tens of thousands from the Dragonpit ruins.
Rank 1 explicitly states that the Great Council of 101 established the precedent that the Iron Throne could not pass to a woman or through a woman to her male descendants.
Rank 2 identifies Queen Visenya's Valyrian steel longsword as Dark Sister.
Rank 1 explicitly states that the dragon Caraxes was called the Blood Wyrm.
Rank 1 identifies Princess Meria Martell as the Yellow Toad of Dorne during the First Dornish War.
Rank 2 explicitly states that Elissa Farman used the gold from the stolen dragon eggs to finance the building of the Sun Chaser.
None of the candidate chunks name or describe the poison used in the assassination of the dragonriders and Ser Hobert Hightower at Tumbleton.
Rank 4 explicitly identifies the squire Pate of Longleaf as the one who mortally wounded Lord Jason Lannister and was knighted as Longleaf the Lionslayer.
Rank 1 mentions Sandoq the Shadow defending Maegor's Holdfast.
Rank 2 names the Seven Speakers who preached to win over the Faithful regarding the royal marriage.
None of the candidate chunks identify the specific location or site of the Butcher's Ball.
Rank 1 explicitly names the blacksmith's bastard who mounted Vermithor as Hugh the Hammer (Hard Hugh).
Rank 1 states that the Shivers of 59 AC killed three Small Council members: Albin Massey, Qarl Corbray, and Grand Maester Benifer.
Rank 1 explains that Lucerys's death ended the war of ravens and envoys and initiated the war of fire and blood in earnest.
None of the candidate chunks describe Addam Velaryon's actions to raise an army and retake Tumbleton to prove his house's loyalty.
Rank 1 details the provisions of the Widow's Law of 52 AC protecting widows from being expelled or impoverished by subsequent heirs.
Rank 1 outlines the terms of the Pact of Ice and Fire betrothing Jacaerys's future firstborn daughter to Cregan Stark's heir Rickon.
Rank 1 details how Queen Helaena's death incited widespread rioting across King's Landing, originating in Flea Bottom.
None of the candidate chunks describe the physical symptoms of Aerea Targaryen's affliction or Barth's theories on Valyria.
None of the candidate chunks describe the Battle Above the Gods Eye ending the line of Aegon I's original dragons with Vhagar's death.
Rank 2 records Larys Strong maneuvering succession politics by advising Aegon II to name Young Aegon as heir.
Rank 2 describes the failure of Peake's strategy when Aegon III bypassed the Hand's daughter to choose Lady Daenaera Velaryon.
